original_question: For a finite abelian group G, let L(G) denote the collection of all sets of factorization lengths arising from G. Can one determine a function f: N -> N such that, whenever |G| >= f(M), the system L(G) contains every finite set L subset N_{>=2} whose width max L - min L is at most M?
target_in_paper: The draft is closest to the chapter's open realization problem in the structure-theorem discussion: whether, for each fixed bound on width, one can realize every finite bounded-width set of integers at least 2 as a set of lengths over some finite abelian group. It does not appear to target the chapter's characterization conjecture, but rather a later open-problem/realization question about small sets of lengths.
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies the main objects: a finite abelian group G, the system L(G) of sets of lengths attached to G, and the idea of realizing all finite sets L with bounded width max L - min L. It also correctly frames the problem as a realization question about which finite subsets of N_{>=2} occur as sets of lengths.
missing_details: The paper-faithful realization question is existential in G for each width bound M; your draft strengthens it to a uniform statement for all groups with |G| large enough, which is broader than the nearest formulation.
L(G) should be understood as the system of sets of lengths of the block monoid B(G), i.e. of zero-sum sequences over G.
One should say explicitly that L is finite and nonempty, with L \subseteq N_{>=2}.
The phrase "L(G) contains L" should be unpacked as: there exists some B in B(G) such that the set of factorization lengths of B is exactly L.
The bounded parameter in the nearest formulation is the width max L - min L; no threshold function f depending on |G| is part of the nearest paper-faithful statement.
To make the question stand alone, one should specify that factorization lengths are taken with respect to factorizations into atoms (minimal zero-sum sequences) in B(G).

If one wants to stay closest to the paper's intent, the question should be phrased as an open realization problem inside the structure-theorem discussion, not as a stronger asymptotic-for-all-large-groups conjecture.
refined_question: For every integer M in N, does there exist a finite abelian group G such that, for every finite nonempty set L \subseteq N_{>=2} with max L - min L <= M, one has L in L(G); equivalently, for every such L there exists a zero-sum sequence B in the block monoid B(G) whose set of factorization lengths is exactly L?
justification: The draft is clearly about realizing bounded-width finite sets as sets of lengths, which places it in the chapter's structure-theorem/open-problem strand rather than in the characterization problem. However, the draft overshoots the nearest paper-faithful formulation by asking for a threshold function f(M) that works for every sufficiently large finite abelian group. The nearest formulation suggested by the chapter's theme is weaker and sharper: for each width bound M, ask only for the existence of some finite abelian group G whose system of sets of lengths realizes every finite nonempty L \subseteq N_{>=2} of width at most M. Because the accessible preview of arXiv:1511.08080 exposes only the abstract and chapter metadata, this identification is necessarily to the nearest realization problem indicated by the chapter's stated focus on the structure theorem and open problems, not to a preview-visible numbered statement.
